# Rule C3: Antagonism By picking an antagonist role you are accepting that you will be expected to be a driving force in the round’s narrative . This means that you should generally try to stick to the expectations of your antagonist role. Deviations are allowed with sufficient roleplay and in-character justification, especially when done to make your impact and role more interesting to the greater narrative.
Players are free to ahelp and request other players to receive an antagonist status when they have rolled an antagonist role by accident.
Given objectives are never mandatory to follow, and act as more of a general suggestion and guideline to your role. Antagonists should aim to complete objectives prior to evacuation.
Players have the freedom to come up with, and modify their own objectives. Modified or replaced objectives must:
-Follow proper escalation (Review B1.4).
-Be within what would reasonably be expected of your role.
-Aim to create an interesting story, and engage with the crew.
-Be sufficiently backed by roleplay justification.
## Rule C3.1: Team antagonists
When playing a team antagonist you must assist your team if possible through gameplay, roleplay, or other methods. Completely disengaging from the team antagonist on both a gameplay and roleplay level is prohibited. Leaving the game via cryosleep or disconnecting is explicitly allowed, as long as an attempt to reduce the negative impact on your team is made, such as handing over important gear, ahelping, etc.
## Rule C3.2: Round-ending antagonists Round-ending antagonists are the only antagonists that should be damaging the station or crew extensively enough to cause an early evacuation.
The following antagonists are considered round-ending:
- Cosmic Cultist - Entropic Colossus - Initial Infected and their Zombies - Nuclear Operative - Revenant - Space Dragon - Syndicate Robo-Neuroticist
A Traitor who receives the “Die a glorious death” objective [color=#ff0000]does not[/color] become round-ending.
## Rule C3.3: Round-removal (RR) Making sure a dead character can’t be revived is considered “round-removal”. Round-removed players are encouraged to make use of the Respawn button and rejoin the round as a different character.
You are under no obligation to ensure the revival of characters you kill in pursuit of an objective or following escalation. With a sound in-character reason and following escalation, you may intentionally round-remove other characters even if they were not your kill target. Bear in mind that characters who died will not remember who killed them (see [textlink="B1.3" link="DeltaVRule1"]).
This rule is intended to allow you to roleplay as an antagonist without having to act against your character’s own interests after hurting someone. It should not be abused to round-remove characters based on sweeping criteria such as employment in a certain department. You should be able to point out a specific current-round action each round-removed character took to justify their round-removal.
